title: Worker runs: How compensation design can curb contagious departures like that at Weil, Gotschal & Manges
desc: The proposed dissolution of Weil, Gotshal & Manges followed an exodus of prominent partners from one of America’s largest law firms. This column explains why such departures can become self-reinforcing and how firms can mitigate the problem through compensation design. Deferred fixed pay, dilutable compensation, and different compensation structures across employees can help firms retain skilled teams at lower cost.

title: Resilience without retreat: How EU firms are redesigning their supply chains
desc: Geopolitical tensions are changing the nature of supply-chain risk. This column presents new survey evidence showing that EU firms increasingly regard trade disruptions as persistent but are moving away from emergency responses such as stockpiling towards longer-term diversification of suppliers and markets. The EU Single Market provides an important buffer against external shocks. At the same time, experimental evidence shows that geopolitical disruptions can have sizeable and asymmetric effects on firms' investment.

title: Gradually, then suddenly – the fiscal value of climate resilience
desc: The human and economic costs of extreme weather events are already large and will grow as temperatures rise further. This column argues that, seen through the lens of the sovereign balance sheet rather than the budget, adaptation reduces the expected fiscal cost of physical climate risk – and the case for investing in it becomes clear.

title: European funds often fall short on currency hedging
desc: The theory of optimal currency hedging has been well established for decades. This column uses new regulatory data to analyse how 2,806 European investment funds use currency forwards and swaps and how the use compares to theoretical benchmarks. It finds that only a minority follow hedging policies close to the portfolio-theory benchmark, and observed derivative trading does not significantly contribute to lower fund risk. Yet a feasible optimal strategy could lower volatility by about 10%, at very modest additional transaction cost.

title: Updating what workers learn: Technology, training content, and the supply of expertise

title: Growth alone is an unlikely fiscal saviour; resolving long-run fiscal tensions in OECD countries also requires expenditure restraint
desc: In public discourse on fiscal tensions across OECD countries, the potential contribution of higher economic growth tends to be overstated. This column argues that long-run fiscal sustainability cannot prudently rely on growth alone. OECD modelling shows that under current policy settings, productivity-led growth provides minimal fiscal relief due to wage linkages, benefit indexation, and relative price effects. Growth from rising labour utilisation is fiscally more potent, but restraining public expenditure is the surest path to long-run fiscal sustainability.
